meta.name: Noir Gallery
meta.notes: Primary fills the main buttons and tints the cursor spotlight; a lightened mix of primary (and of accent for tag dots) draws the thin hairlines, room numbers and italic accents, so even navy or near-black brands stay visible on the dark canvas.

issues: Scores before (1-10): creativity 6, typography 8, layout & rhythm 3, polish 3, brand-colour robustness 7, mobile 4, generic-template feel 6.

Fatal: everything below 'The halls' rendered as a black void on desktop, mobile and stress. The curtain/fade reveals depended only on IntersectionObserver with a 10% threshold, so doors, works, story, salon, quote and contact stayed hidden at clip-path inset(50%) / opacity 0.
Catalog: every product image was invisible for the same reason, so the plinths were empty grey boxes.

Horizontal overflow on all three home renders: the hero light cone (left/right -40%, top -60vh), the rotated side caption and a fixed grain layer at inset -50% pushed the page wider than the viewport.
The cursor spotlight, which is the signature interaction, barely registered: an 8% screen-blend glow on near-black is close to invisible, so the page never felt like a dark room being lit.
The brief asks for images hung with museum labels, but the salon only had a tiny 'Fig. n' caption. Only the hero had a real label.
Catalog: 3 works were pinned in a 4-column auto-fill grid, leaving a dead quarter of the page on the right. The plinths read as cards rather than pedestals.
fixed: Rebuilt the reveal logic on both pages. IntersectionObserver threshold dropped to 1%, plus a sweep on scroll, resize and load that lights anything already above the fold line. Headless renders (navigator.webdriver), reduced-motion users and browsers without IntersectionObserver get the fully revealed page. The clip-path curtain still plays for real visitors.
Removed the overflow: html gets overflow-x:clip, the hero clips its light cone and side caption (overflow:hidden), and the grain layer is now inset:0.

Made the spotlight much stronger by adding a 'darkness' layer: a fixed radial vignette tied to the same --x/--y cursor variables (and to the auto-drifting path on touch devices) that darkens everything outside the cone of light. The room now visibly brightens wherever the cursor goes, on both pages.

Every salon image now has a cream museum label overlapping the frame: a brand-colour hairline tab, 'Fig. n · Room V' in spaced small caps, and the brand name and year in italic. Labels alternate left and right to make a salon-hang rhythm, and fade in after the curtain.
Catalog: the grid uses auto-fit with a max width, and a 3-work collection gets a centred, staggered triptych. Plinths gain a hairline top edge and a shadow pooling on the floor beneath each pedestal.
